papers.title: Optimal Design of Baffle in Liquid-Filled Tank Subjected to Sloshing using XFEM and Bayesian Optimization
papers.venue: HAL (Le Centre pour la Communication Scientifique Directe)

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文将贝叶斯优化与XFEM结合用于液体晃动问题，其方法可迁移至植入物设计中的约束优化与不确定性量化。
llm.why_not_core: No biomedical context, no implant mechanics, no FEA surrogate for solid mechanics.

summary_zh.motivation: 提高液体晃动问题中挡板设计的优化效率。
summary_zh.method: 采用扩展有限元法(XFEM)与贝叶斯优化结合进行设计优化。
summary_zh.result: 实现了高效且准确的挡板最优设计。
summary_zh.validation: 通过数值模拟案例验证优化方法有效性。

summary_en.motivation: To improve the optimization efficiency of baffle design in liquid-filled tanks under sloshing.
summary_en.method: Combined extended finite element method (XFEM) with Bayesian optimization for design optimization.
summary_en.result: Achieved efficient and accurate optimal baffle design.
summary_en.validation: Validated the optimization method through numerical simulation cases.

papers.title: Bioprinting High-Cell-Density Cardiac Tissue Constructs With Sustained Contractile Function.
papers.abstract: The development of in vitro models that reflect key elements of cardiac physiology remains a major challenge for assessing cardiotoxicity and drug efficacy. Tissue engineering approaches, together with advanced biofabrication technologies, provide a new way to recreate the target tissue composition and organization, enabling the development of 3D in vitro models able to mimic the biological function of the target tissue. Here, we present a novel 3D bioprinted cardiac in vitro model fabricated using reactive jet impingement (ReJI), an advanced biofabrication technique that enables rapid, high-resolution deposition of living cells within a bespoke hydrogel matrix composed of type I collagen, alginate, and fibrin. Using the murine HL-1 cardiomyocyte cell line, we demonstrate for the first time that ReJI bioprinting supports the formation of stable, functional 3D cardiac constructs exhibiting spontaneous and sustained contractility over 21 days, without external stimulation. The 3D models expressed key biomarkers related to cell contraction: desmin, myosin, and gap junction alpha-1 (GJA1). In particular, cultures showed increased early-stage expression of GJA1, indicative of the formation of gap junction structures within the 3D culture, and were susceptible to drug-induced dysrhythmia, confirming their significant potential for use in cardiotoxicity testing.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文聚焦于生物打印心脏组织构建，未涉及AI在生物打印中的应用。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not incorporate AI/ML into any bioprinting workflow stage, nor does it address autonomous decision-making or experimental validation of AI models.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发能模拟心脏生理功能的体外模型用于药物测试。
summary_zh.method: 使用反应射流冲击生物打印技术构建高细胞密度心脏组织。
summary_zh.result: 构建物自发持续收缩21天，表达关键生物标志物并对药物反应敏感。
summary_zh.validation: 通过免疫荧光和药物诱导心律失常实验验证功能。

summary_en.motivation: To create in vitro cardiac models that recapitulate key physiological features for cardiotoxicity and drug efficacy assessment.
summary_en.method: Reactive jet impingement bioprinting was used to fabricate high-cell-density cardiac constructs within a collagen-alginate-fibrin hydrogel.
summary_en.result: The bioprinted constructs exhibited spontaneous and sustained contractility for 21 days, expressed cardiac biomarkers, and responded to drug-induced dysrhythmia.
summary_en.validation: Functional validation was performed via immunostaining for desmin, myosin, and GJA1, and by demonstrating susceptibility to drug-induced dysrhythmia.
